summary: Defines a basic set of managed objects for SNMP-based event notification management of DOCSIS-compliant cable modems and cable modem termination systems. It is a standards-track MIB document.

eli5.summary: When a cable modem notices a problem, it writes it in a log. This defines how those event notes are kept and reported so a technician can read them.

questions: what is the docsis event notification mib
what snmp notifications does a cable modem send
how to enable docsis snmp notifications
subtitle: A standard set of SNMP notifications that cable modems and their head-end systems can send when DOCSIS events happen.

tldr.problem: Cable operators manage thousands of DOCSIS devices with SNMP, but only a minimal set of standard SNMP notifications existed for reporting what goes wrong on them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a MIB module with one notification for each DOCSIS event category, split into a group for cable modems and a group for cable modem termination systems, plus two bit-mask objects that switch individual notifications on or off.
tldr.outcome: Devices SHOULD support this minimum set so operators can monitor events through SNMP. The RFC has since been updated by RFC 9141.

today: RFC 4547 is a Proposed Standard that has been updated by RFC 9141. Read the update alongside it for the current state of this MIB module.

sections.title: Why DOCSIS Needs Event Notifications
sections.content:
RFC 4547 defines a MIB module (a collection of managed objects read through the Simple Network Management Protocol, SNMP) for event notification on DOCSIS-compliant cable modems (CMs) and cable modem termination systems (CMTSs). It is written as an extension of the DOCSIS Cable Device MIB.

The overview says DOCSIS devices were being deployed at a rate of multiple thousands per day, and that operators were struggling to manage them. They already used SNMP, MIBs required by DOCSIS and SNMP notifications, and using notifications to report events was becoming more popular. The catch was that only a minimal set of SNMP notifications was available.

This MIB, together with the DOCSIS operations support specifications it cites, provides a minimum set of standard notifications that DOCSIS devices SHOULD support. Appendix H of the DOCSIS 1.1 specification and Appendix D of the DOCSIS 2.0 specification define the required events, and the notifications here are how those events are reported over SNMP.
sections.eli5: Lots of cable modems were being set up, and the people running them needed a standard way to hear about problems. This RFC gives every modem the same set of alarm bells.

sections.title: DOCSIS Vocabulary
sections.content:
The RFC includes a short glossary of cable terms. A CM is the "slave" station in a DOCSIS cable data system. A CMTS is the master station, found in a head-end. It is the only station that transmits downstream, and it controls the scheduling of upstream transmissions by its CMs.

Downstream is the direction from the CMTS to the CM, and upstream is the direction from the CM to the CMTS. The head-end is the origination point of subscriber video signals in most cable systems.

Other glossary entries cover the Baseline Privacy Interface (data privacy over the HFC network in DOCSIS 1.0), its Plus version (which adds CM authentication), the SID (Service ID, which identifies an upstream bandwidth allocation and class of service) and TLV (Type/Length/Value encoding).
sections.eli5: The modem at your house is the follower, and the big box at the cable company is the leader. Messages going to your house go down, and messages from your house go up.

sections.title: Structure of the Notification MIB
sections.content:
The module is named DOCS-IETF-CABLE-DEVICE-NOTIFICATION-MIB, and it is designed to extend the notification module of RFC 2669. Its identity is docsDevNotifMIB, registered at { mib-2 132 }.

Two groups of notifications are defined: one for cable modem events and one for CMTS events. DOCSIS assigns each event to a functional category, and the MIB defines a notification for each category. The variable-binding list of each notification carries information about the event that happened on the device.

The module has a control branch (docsDevNotifControl), a CM notification branch (docsDevCmNotifs) and a CMTS notification branch (docsDevCmtsNotifs). It imports definitions from the SMIv2 modules, the DOCS-CABLE-DEVICE-MIB, the DOCS-IF-MIB and the IF-MIB.
sections.eli5: The alarms are sorted into two boxes. One box holds alarms for modems, and the other holds alarms for the cable company's big machine.

sections.title: The Notifications and Their Contents
sections.content:
There are 16 CM notifications. They cover an unknown TLV during parsing, failed dynamic service requests, responses and acknowledgements, Baseline Privacy initialization and key management problems, dynamic security association problems, DHCP failure, software upgrade start, failure, success and code verification certificate failure, time of day failure, and failed dynamic channel change requests, responses and acknowledgements.

There are 12 CMTS notifications. They cover failed initial registration requests, responses and acknowledgements, failed dynamic service messages, Baseline Privacy initialization and key management problems, dynamic security association problems, and failed dynamic channel change messages.

Each CM notification reports the event priority level (docsDevEvLevel), the event identifier (docsDevEvId), a text description (docsDevEvText), the cable interface MAC address of the modem, the MAC address of the CMTS it is connected to, the highest DOCSIS version the device supports, the QoS level it is operating in and its upstream modulation type. Some notifications add objects specific to the event, such as software file name and server for upgrade events.
sections.eli5: Each alarm says what went wrong, how serious it is, and which modem it is about, so the technician does not have to guess.

sections.title: Switching Notifications On and Off
sections.content:
Two read-write objects control which notifications are sent. docsDevCmNotifControl is a BITS object with one bit per CM notification (bits 0 to 15), and docsDevCmtsNotifControl has one bit per CMTS notification (bits 0 to 11). If a bit is set, that notification is enabled. If it is not set, the notification is disabled.

The default value of both objects is the empty set, so everything starts off. If the device is rebooted, the value SHOULD revert to the default.

The RFC also notes that notifications are under the control of the MIB modules defined in RFC 3413 as well, so this bit mask is not the only switch.
sections.eli5: Every alarm has its own light switch. All the switches start off, and the technician flips on the ones they care about.

sections.title: Compliance Statements
sections.content: The module defines two compliance statements. A CM that claims compliance must implement docsDevCmNotifControlGroup (the control object) and docsDevCmNotificationGroup (the 16 notifications). A CMTS must implement docsDevCmtsNotifControlGroup and docsDevCmtsNotificationGroup (the 12 notifications).
sections.eli5: A modem that wants the gold star has to have all of its alarms and their switches. The same goes for the big machine at the cable company.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The two control objects are the only read-write objects, and they may be sensitive. Setting them can cause flooding of notifications, which can disrupt network service. It can also mean that notifications are not emitted when the operator intends them to be.

The notifications themselves reveal information about the network, including event priority, event ID, event text, CM capability and QoS level, upstream modulation type and MAC addresses. Monitoring them could be used to gather information about the state of the network and devices.

SNMP versions before SNMPv3 did not include adequate security. The RFC recommends considering the SNMPv3 security features, including its cryptographic mechanisms for authentication and privacy, and says deploying SNMP versions before SNMPv3 is NOT RECOMMENDED. Operators must configure access so that only legitimate principals can read or change the objects.
sections.eli5: If a stranger could flip the alarm switches, they could make the alarms ring nonstop or stay quiet. So only the right people should be allowed to touch them.

sections.title: IANA Registration
sections.content: The only IANA action is the object identifier for the module. The descriptor docsDevNotifMIB is recorded in the SMI Numbers registry with the value { mib-2 132 }.
sections.eli5: The module got its own official number in a big list, so nobody else uses the same one.
